Sasha (pagerbot): :rotating_light: PagerDuty: redwood-prod -> critical: inference-queue-saturation fired (PD-54321) <https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD-54321|view incident>

Alex M: ACKing — I'm on this. seeing a big tail in the embeddings queue, high enqueue latency.

Alex M: quick snapshot from the dashboard: `queue_length ~ 12k`, `p95 latency 1.8s`, tokens/sec dropped ~40% vs baseline.

Priya K: curious if it's the prefix caching layer or a downstream datastore? any 5xxs?

Mike R: logs show a lot of `KVCache::miss` spikes and `grpc deadline exceeded` to redis-cluster-1 around 15:02 UTC.

Jordan S: tagging runbook: <https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/inference-queue-saturation|runbook: queued requests>. Step 1: scale worker pool. I'm starting an emergency scale now.

Alex M: starting with non-disruptive measures: 1) enable fallback routing to model-compact-v2 for low-priority traffic, 2) increase worker pool by +30% in eu-west region, 3) enable caching bypass metrics.

oncall-bot: PagerDuty ack recorded: PD-54321 acknowledged by Alex M at 2025-06-12T15:03:12Z

Priya K: I can take ownership if you need to rotate. I'll open a small bridge.

Alex M: please do — will handoff in ~20m. Current mitigation: `kubectl scale deployment/inference-workers --replicas=26 -n prod` (eu-west) — executed.

Mike R: confirmed workers scaling succeeded, new pods coming up. Also increased redis replicas from 3 -> 4 (hot patch) to reduce grpc timeouts.

Priya K: joining bridge now: zoom.us/j/xxxxx (ops bridge).

Alex M: running a targeted routing rewrite to divert traffic from long-tail clients: `route-rule set --service inference --match 'client_tier:free' --backend model=compact-v2 --priority=25` — pushing.

Sasha (pagerbot): auto-update: capacity policy triggered autoscaler (eu-west) +30% at 15:05 UTC.

Jordan S: telemetry looks better but still elevated. p95 down to 1.1s, queue_length ~5.2k. partial relief.

Priya K: customer impact check — support showed a spike in latency complaints from two small customers (cust-zenco, cust-hyve). No major enterprise SLAs affected yet. Marking customer-impact=limited.

Alex M: documenting temporary mitigation choices in incident doc: compact-v2 route & redis replica bump. Need to monitor for regression in quality for routed traffic.

Mike R: note: saw ~4% increased error rate in model outputs for some prompts under compact-v2, likely expected. Logging flagged prompts for eval.

Priya K: cross-checking regen rates. Deciding to backfill KV cache from snapshot to reduce misses — initiating `cache-restore --snapshot s20250612-a` (long-running).

Alex M: heading offline for a call at 15:20 — handing ownership to Priya. Priya, can you own until stable?

Priya K: I have it. Will ping every 10m. Alex — thanks, go ahead. :+1:

Sasha (pagerbot): PagerDuty: PD-54321 reassigned to Priya K by Alex M at 2025-06-12T15:18:47Z

Priya K: quick status — autoscaler and redis bump helped. queue_length trending down to ~900. cache-restore ~40% complete. No new customer complaints in last 10m.

Jordan S: recommending a temporary throttle on low-priority batch jobs to keep headroom. Executing `cgroups throttle batch-jobs 60%`.

Priya K: applied throttle. side-effect: batch throughput drops but latency improves for online calls.

Mike R: observed one node with OOM kill during scale — evacuated and cycled. No data loss. Documenting hardware blip.

Priya K: status ping 15:40 UTC — queue_length 300, p95 0.42s, errors down to baseline. Starting to remove emergency routing after verifying compact-v2 quality sample.

Priya K: `route-rule remove --service inference --match 'client_tier:free'` — rollout in progress.

Sasha (pagerbot): PagerDuty note: PD-54321 status changed to monitoring (auto) at 2025-06-12T15:50:03Z

Alex M: back — thanks for the smooth handoff. Any outstanding customer messages we should send?

Priya K: support draft: "We experienced temporary inference latency increases affecting a small subset of low-volume customers between 15:00–15:45 UTC. We've applied mitigations and performance has returned to normal. We're following up with the impacted customers with details." Open to edits.

Jordan S: looks good. add a note about permanent follow-up: we'll run a regression eval on compact-v2 routing and consider cache pre-warming.

Mike R: next actions: postmortem owner = Alex M, follow-up action owner = Jordan S (redis cluster hardening), and Priya K (runbook update and autoscale tuning).

Priya K: changing PD status to resolved after 15m of stable metrics.

Sasha (pagerbot): PagerDuty: PD-54321 resolved by Priya K at 2025-06-12T15:58:00Z

Alex M: thanks team. I'll open the postmortem doc and include timeline, mitigation commands, and customer-impact table.

Priya K: closing notes: please add any logs or traces to the incident doc. Will schedule a 30m postmortem sync tomorrow. :calendar:

Jordan S: thumbs up. Great job triaging quickly and coordinating fallback routing.

Mike R: nice one. Learned some useful perf signals.

Sasha (pagerbot): System: incident thread archived.
